note: Supersession fixture for the moving-count case. One check-suite count moves 214 -> 226 -> 238 -> 241 (LAN) -> 251 -> 247 -> 251 -> 262 -> 334/341 -> 358/371 across twelve chunks, restated in wording that drifts between a heavy boilerplate form and plain prose, with tool output repeating retired counts, a separate lint step, a durable fact about the suite file, a wrong README number, and an inventory line sharing the project name. The expected end state is one active offline count and one active LAN count; every other count retired. Content is invented: a queue-drain CLI called tctl, no hostnames, no absolute paths, no credentials. Each chunk also declares the facts a correct writer should hold, and marks a statement stale when it records a superseded number rather than asserting a current one. dev/run.ts reads only `text`; `facts` is the contract the outcome report grades against.
